title: A heat pump at its Carnot limit
caption: Moving heat from 0 °C (273.15 K) to 35 °C radiators (308.15 K): COP_max = T_h/(T_h − T_c) = 308/35 = 8.8. Each 1.0 kW of electrical work delivers 8.8 kW of heat to the house, because 7.8 kW is simply carried in from the outdoor air. A real machine reaches about 3–4.
alt: Energy flow: 1.0 kW of electricity plus 7.8 kW of heat from outdoors give 8.8 kW of heat to the radiators; COP 8.8.
description: Heat taken from the cold outdoors: Q_c = Q_h − W = 7.8 kW.
Heat delivered at 35 °C: Q_h = COP × W = 8.8 × 1.0 = 8.8 kW. Energy is conserved: Q_h = W + Q_c.
